title: Prologue: The Poet Returns to Complete the Book
english: You have all hope, O Emperor, by adding the lacking part to the new woven-roofed palace. So then, best of men, suitably and now I come, adding the missing part to the book. For it would be beautiful if the words co-create with the Master the new house of the Word. Well then, O theater, well then the eagerness toward the better; for I do not think that now the mind attends to me, but for the sake of the new house there will be a theater and a festival again. Well then, O theater; for thrice already summoning and raising up from accustomed labors I have not yet seen anyone of you gloomy, none accounting idleness more urgent than works. For there is nothing small, nor if it is small, of the works of the greatest King and of the new house that wrought all grace to us, long festivals of pious men; who to all brought serious joy, stirred all reasonable delight, as of spring appearing, winter having departed, already then every shoot bears harmonious sound of varied melody. Nothing is small of the new house; for it is truly a sight of all-giving luxury. Therefore I approach the revered place, which the Emperor wrought in his presence most beautifully as a place for the books of the mystagogues of the sacred words.
